t.1.207.1: Having told all that to the brāhmaṇas, O Bhārata, the son of the wielder of the thunderbolt then set out for the flank of the Himālaya.
t.1.207.3: At the sacred fords and at the holy shrines he gave away thousands of cows, and that best of the Kurus also gave dwellings to the twice-born.
t.1.207.4: And having bathed at the tīrtha of Hiraṇyabindu, the best of men beheld the foremost of mountains and its holy sanctuaries.
t.1.207.2: Having reached the Banyan of Agastya and the mountain of Vasiṣṭha, and at Bhṛgutuṅga, the son of Kuntī performed the purification of himself.
t.1.207.5: Having come down, O Bhārata, that best of men, the bull among the Bharatas, set out with the brāhmaṇas, eager to reach the eastern region.
t.1.207.6: One after another, the best of the Kurus saw the sacred fords, and the lovely river Utpalinī on the way toward the Naimiṣa forest.
t.1.207.8: Thus, beholding all the sacred fords and likewise the hermitages, and purifying himself, he gave wealth to the brahmins.
t.1.207.7: The Nandā and the Aparanandā, the glorious Kauśikī, the Mahānadī, Gayā, and the Gaṅgā as well, O Bhārata.
t.1.207.9: Whatever holy places there were among the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas and Kaliṅgas, he went to all of them, the tīrthas and the sanctuaries alike. And having seen them according to the prescribed rite, he then gave away wealth as well.
t.1.207.10: At the gates of the Kaliṅga kingdom, O Bhārata, the brahmins who had followed the Pāṇḍava took leave of Kaunteya and turned back.
t.1.207.12: Having passed beyond the Kaliṅgas, the lord went on, gazing upon lands and sanctuaries that were holy and delightful.
t.1.207.11: But the hero Dhanaṃjaya, son of Kuntī, having been given leave by them, set out with a few companions along the way that led to the ocean.
t.1.207.13: Having seen Mount Mahendra, adorned with ascetics, he went slowly along the seashore to Maṇalūra.
t.1.207.14: There, having visited all the holy tīrthas and sacred shrines, the mighty-armed one approached the lord of the earth, O king, Citravāhana, the ruler of Maṇalūra, a knower of dharma.
t.1.207.15: He had a daughter named Citrāṅgadā, lovely to behold. He saw her by chance as she was wandering about in that city.
t.1.207.17: In this lineage there was a king named Prabhaṃkara. Being sonless and desiring offspring, he performed the highest austerity.
t.1.207.16: Seeing that fair-hipped daughter of Citravāhana, he desired her, and approaching the king, he made known his purpose. Then the king spoke these words to him, gently and conciliatingly.
t.1.207.19: The Blessed One granted him a single offspring in each generation of his line; therefore in this family there is always but one offspring at a time.
t.1.207.18: By that fierce austerity and by that prostration, Śaṃkara, the Lord, Mahādeva, the husband of Umā, was gratified by him.
t.1.207.20: To all those forefathers of mine sons were born; but to me this daughter was born, who will surely be the one to perpetuate the lineage.
t.1.207.21: "She is my son": such is my resolve, O best of men; by the rule laid down for this purpose she has been designated a putrikā, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.207.23: Having promised, "So be it," and having accepted that maiden, Kaunteya dwelt in that city for three years.
t.1.207.22: Let this be her bride-price: let one who continues the lineage be born here. On this condition, accept her, O Pāṇḍava.
